problem: Prior VLN memory representations lose information about the visited environment. Recurrent states compress history into one vector. Topological maps (e.g., DUET) keep only node-level features and cannot represent spatial relations among objects and scenes. Top-down semantic maps (e.g., CM2, VLMaps) are limited to predefined labels, so they cannot represent unlisted objects (e.g., 'refrigerator') or attributes ('wood table', 'blue couch'). BEVBert's metric map is local, covering only two steps of observations.
motivation: Instruction grounding needs a global, spatially precise memory of everything seen so far, with open-vocabulary, fine-grained visual detail rather than coarse node or semantic-class features. Two observations drive the design. Grid (patch) features from CLIP carry a much richer semantic space than detected objects or semantic labels. Each map cell can accumulate hundreds of features (more than 600 by the end of an episode), so cells must be aggregated selectively by instruction relevance rather than averaged.
key_idea: Project CLIP patch features from every past panorama, via depth and pose, into a global grid memory that is re-rendered at each step as an egocentric, dynamically growing N×N top-down map. Each cell is aggregated by instruction-relevance attention, and the map is fused with a DUET-style trajectory graph for local and global action prediction.
insight: A fine-grained, open-vocabulary visual metric memory beats both topological and semantic maps under an otherwise identical model. On R2R-CE val-unseen (Table 5): GridMM reaches 49.05 SR / 40.99 SPL, versus DUET topological map 47.02/38.86, object-feature map 47.61/40.13, top-down semantic map 46.36/38.41, and no map 45.19/37.82. The semantic map even underperforms the topological map, which the authors attribute to a feature gap with the panoramic visual features. Ablations (Table 6) show each component helps: removing the trajectory memory drops SR to 47.42, average-pooling cells instead of instruction-relevance aggregation drops it to 48.63, and using absolute instead of egocentric coordinates drops it to 48.72. A larger map resolution (20×20) helps further (49.86 SR / 42.52 SPL) at higher compute cost.
method: Grid memory: at each step, CLIP-ViT-B/32 patch (grid) features of the K panorama views are stored with absolute 2D coordinates. The coordinates are computed from downsized depth, view heading and agent position, and the memory M_t = M_{t-1} ∪ new features grows over time.

Egocentric dynamic map: all stored features are transformed each step into a coordinate frame centered at the agent, with the y-axis along its heading. Side length is L_t = 2·max(|x_rel|, |y_rel|) over all features, so the map grows with the explored area and is divided into N×N cells (N=14 by default).

Instruction-relevance aggregation: each cell's features get a relevance matrix A = (F W1)(W' W2)^T against the instruction tokens. A max over tokens, then a softmax over the cell's features, gives weights for a weighted sum of linearly projected features. Distance and heading (sin/cos) embeddings of the cell center relative to the agent are added.

Observation and trajectory encoding: panorama view features (ViT-B/16 ImageNet) carry angle, distance and start-relative embeddings plus a stop token and pass through a 2-layer transformer. A DUET-like trajectory memory holds average-pooled features of visited waypoints plus candidate-waypoint view features, with distance, heading and step embeddings.

Two-stage cross-modal reasoning: a 1-layer cross-modal encoder fuses [map; trajectory] with the instruction, supervised by the HER loss. A 4-layer encoder (cross-attention then self-attention) then uses [panorama; trajectory] as queries over [instruction; trajectory; map]. Local and global action scores come from separate FFNs and are fused with a DUET-style sigmoid gate.

Training: layers are initialized from LXMERT (language 9, panorama 2, map/trajectory 1, cross-modal 4; hidden 768). Pre-training uses MLM, MVM, SAP, and Historical Environment Reasoning (HER: predict the next action from map+trajectory only). Fine-tuning uses DAgger with a shortest-path pseudo-demonstrator.

Continuous transfer: in R2R-CE/RxR-CE, the Bridging pre-trained waypoint predictor proposes navigable waypoints, and the model pre-trained on discrete R2R is fine-tuned in Habitat. Feature caching of projections and relevance terms reduces FLOPs below BEVBert.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-initialized multi-layer transformer (trained/fine-tuned) + frozen CLIP-ViT-B/32 grid features + ViT-B/16 (ImageNet) view features
setting.training_data: R2R: R2R + PREVALENT augmented data (Hao et al. 2020) for pre-training, then fine-tuning. REVERIE: REVERIE + DUET-synthesized augmented data. SOON: original data with automatically cleaned object boxes. R2R-CE: R2R-pretrained model fine-tuned on R2R-CE. RxR-CE training details not given.
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (MP3D); in continuous envs, waypoints predicted by the Bridging waypoint predictor, executed with low-level controls
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R, REVERIE, SOON); Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE)
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard settings: nav graph in discrete envs, provided candidate object boxes in REVERIE, BUTD-detected boxes in SOON; agent pose (GPS) and depth are used for map projection

DUET transferred to R2R-CE is labeled '(Ours)' but is a baseline reimplementation and is excluded here.
results: GridMM sets or ties the state of the art on all five benchmarks. On REVERIE test-unseen it reaches 53.13 SR / 36.60 SPL / 34.87 RGS / 23.45 RGSPL, versus BEVBert 52.81/36.41/32.06/22.09 and DUET 52.51/36.06/31.88/22.06. On REVERIE val-unseen it improves on DUET by +4.39 SR, though its SR is slightly below BEVBert (51.37 vs 51.78). On R2R it ties BEVBert (75/64 val-unseen, 73/62 test SR/SPL). On SOON val-unseen it beats DUET (37.46 vs 36.28 SR), though test SPL is marginally lower (21.25 vs 21.42). In continuous environments it clearly outperforms prior work: R2R-CE test-unseen 46 SR / 39 SPL versus Bridging-VLNBERT 42/36 and Sim-2-Sim 44/37, and RxR-CE 36.26 SR versus a transferred DUET at 29.93.
limitations: The authors state that handling multi-floor environments remains open: the map is a single 2D top-down plane.
Performance improves with map resolution (20×20 > 14×14), but compute grows, so the default is a compromise. The method also relies on depth and accurate pose to project features.
Gains in discrete environments over BEVBert are marginal (ties on R2R, slightly lower val-unseen SR/RGS on REVERIE), and all ablations are reported only on R2R-CE val-unseen.
